solution:
A triplet of natural numbers is Pythagorean when the square of the largest equals the sum of the squares of the other two.
Test \((3, 4, 5)\): \(3^2 + 4^2 = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5^2\).
The others fail: \(1^2 + 5^2 = 26 \ne 10^2\), \(2^2 + 2^2 = 8 \ne 2^2\), \(2^2 + 5^2 = 29 \ne 5^2\).
Hence the Pythagorean triplet is \((3, 4, 5)\).

By Pythagoras' theorem the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the two sides making the right angle.
So \((\text{hypotenuse})^2 = 169\).
\(\therefore\) hypotenuse \(= \sqrt{169} = 13\).
The length of the hypotenuse is \(13\).

Read each date as the triplet (day, month, year) and test the definition of a Pythagorean triplet.
\(15/08/17 \Rightarrow 15^2 + 8^2 = 225 + 64 = 289 = 17^2\), so it is a Pythagorean triplet.
The rest fail: \(8^2 + 16^2 = 320 \ne 16^2\); \(3^2 + 5^2 = 34 \ne 17^2\); \(4^2 + 9^2 = 97 \ne 15^2\).
Hence the required date is \(15/08/17\).

Here the square of one side equals the sum of the squares of the remaining two sides, since \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\).
By the converse of Pythagoras' theorem, such a triangle is right angled, the right angle being opposite side \(c\).
Hence the triangle is a right angled triangle.

A diagonal of a square makes two \(45^\circ-45^\circ-90^\circ\) triangles, the diagonal being the hypotenuse.
By the \(45^\circ-45^\circ-90^\circ\) property, side \(= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times 10\sqrt{2} = 10\) cm.
(Equivalently, by Pythagoras' theorem \(2s^2 = (10\sqrt{2})^2 = 200\), so \(s = 10\) cm.)
\(\therefore\) perimeter \(= 4 \times 10 = 40\) cm.

The altitude to the hypotenuse is the geometric mean of the two segments it cuts on the hypotenuse.
By the theorem of geometric mean, \((\text{altitude})^2 = 4 \times 9 = 36\).
\(\therefore\) altitude \(= \sqrt{36} = 6\) cm.
The length of the altitude is \(6\) cm.

The height and the base are the two sides making the right angle.
By Pythagoras' theorem, \((\text{hypotenuse})^2 = 24^2 + 18^2 = 576 + 324 = 900\).
\(\therefore\) hypotenuse \(= \sqrt{900} = 30\) cm.
The hypotenuse is \(30\) cm.

In \(\triangle ABC\), \(BC^2 + AB^2 = 6^2 + (6\sqrt{3})^2 = 36 + 108 = 144 = 12^2 = AC^2\).
By the converse of Pythagoras' theorem the angle opposite AC is a right angle, so \(\angle B = 90^\circ\) and AC is the hypotenuse.
Now \(BC = 6 = \frac{1}{2} \times 12 = \frac{1}{2}AC\), and BC is the side opposite \(\angle A\).
In a right angled triangle a side that is half the hypotenuse has \(30^\circ\) opposite it, so \(\angle A = 30^\circ\).
